item.title: Apple Tests Daily Usage Limits for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence Features
item.description:
Apple Tests Daily Usage Limits for Siri AI and Apple Intelligence Features

Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3, using the updates to test new per-device daily usage limits for select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features.

🧩 How it works

Basic Siri commands and requests remain free and unlimited. However, advanced features relying on cloud-based processing are subject to daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage:

  • Using Siri AI for multi-step, personal context requests
  • Image generation and editing tools
  • Automations in Shortcuts that rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models
  • Third-party apps that use those same cloud models

Apple has not specified exactly how many times these features can be used before limits are reached, noting that limits will vary based on the task. The company plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and when they have finally reached it.

⚙️ Key details

Frequent users of these features will require an iCloud Plus subscription to avoid limits. Instead of waiting until midnight for usage to reset, most existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) include higher daily limits at the same price:

Plan Monthly Cost Usage Multiplier
200GB $2.99 2x
2TB $9.99 5x
6TB $29.99 10x
12TB $59.99 20x

Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that is used on a first-come, first-served basis.

#Apple #Siri #AppleIntelligence #iCloud #UsageLimits

Source: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions

item.title: Meta’s Muse assistant clarifies message‑preview access on new Mac app
item.description:
Meta’s Muse assistant clarifies message‑preview access on new Mac app

Meta’s Muse AI assistant explained how it accesses message data on its new Mac app.

🔍 Overview

  • Muse is an AI assistant paired with a new Mac app that can access Messages, Calendar, and Notes.
  • In a public interaction, Muse said it “I saw the notification previews, not your message history.” and “I haven’t been reading your texts.”

🧩 How it works

  • The Mac app exposes notifications as a capability; notifications arrive to Muse through device sync.
  • When a user enables access, Muse syncs data from Messages; otherwise it only sees notification previews.
  • Muse admitted, “Honest answer: I can’t give you the exact plumbing,” and added, “What I know is that the paired Mac app exposes notifications as one of its capabilities, and they arrive to me through the device sync.”

⚙️ Permissions & Clarifications

  • Required permissions include granting the Mac app full disk access.
  • Features are opt‑in, as stated by David Singleton of Meta Superintelligence Labs.
  • Singleton clarified that Muse “does not watch notifications on your Mac, but rather syncs data from Messages only after the user has specifically enabled access.”
  • In Jason Aten’s screenshots, Muse gave an incorrect explanation of the notification‑sync feature.

💡 Why it matters

  • The exchange highlights the difference between reading notification previews and full message history.
  • It underscores Meta’s approach to make data access optional and transparent for users.

#Meta #AIassistant #MacApp #Privacy

Source: Meta’s Muse is creepy, but maybe not for the reasons you think
